segments.source: Jaguar is a useful small-bag trial if you want a dark espresso that Equator expressly builds for both straight shots and milk. Its current page names two Honduran components and a wet-hulled Sumatran component, giving unusually concrete blend context. The chocolate, spice, apricot and hazelnut notes belong to Equator; older independent and owner opinions do not prove the result of your next bag.

segments.context: Intelligentsia Coffee · United StatesBlack Cat Analog EspressoChoose Analog over Black Cat Classic when you want Intelligentsia's more traditional, chocolate-led espresso brief and make milk drinks regularly. segments.source: Verve Aster 12-ounce whole-bean package
segments.context: Verve Coffee Roasters · United StatesAsterAster is the Verve blend to trial if you want an Ethiopian fruit-and-sugar brief with published starts for both concentrated espresso and filter. Verve says it blends coffee from one origin roasted two ways; that is not the same as one fixed single-origin lot. Nectarine, key lime and brown sugar are roaster notes. Owner enthusiasm is limited and older, so a dated small bag is the sensible first purchase.Updated 2026-11-10 · Check current US whole-bean price at November 10, 2026

segments.source: Verve Bronson French Roast 12-ounce whole-bean package
segments.context: Verve Coffee Roasters · United StatesBronson French RoastBronson is the Verve option to try when a dark cup with cream or sugar is the actual goal. The current page calls it the roaster's darkest blend, lists Colombia and Central America, and publishes Dwell, French press and Chemex starts. It does not publish a Bronson-specific espresso recipe, so its dark roast alone is not evidence of espresso behavior. A few older owner comments cannot predict a new bag.Updated 2026-11-10 · Check current US whole-bean price at November 10, 2026
